blocks.text: 1. Continual Learning

Federated Learning's own closing recap, already covered in Federated Learning, pointed forward here. Continual Learning, exploring how a model can keep learning new tasks without forgetting old ones, tackles a genuinely important, long-term challenge.
It genuinely trains on a genuinely sequence of tasks over time, retaining earlier skills while gaining new ones, a goal explored in full throughout this topic.

3. Recapping Catastrophic Forgetting

blocks.alt: A new task learned can cause an old task to be forgotten

blocks.text: This connects back to catastrophic forgetting, already covered generally in Full Fine-Tuning. Full fine-tuning already genuinely warned that updating every weight on new data risks overwriting old knowledge.
Continual learning genuinely exists specifically to systematically genuinely solve exactly that risk, the exact core motivation explored throughout the rest of this topic.
4. Sequential Task Arrival

blocks.alt: Task 1 arrives, then task 2 arrives later, then task 3 arrives later still

blocks.text: This connects back to recapping catastrophic forgetting, already covered in this topic. Genuinely real continual learning settings genuinely present tasks one after another, never all genuinely at once.
Each genuinely new task genuinely must be learned without genuinely revisiting earlier tasks' own full original data, the exact defining structure explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 5. Regularization Based Approaches

blocks.alt: Important weights are protected from change

blocks.text: This connects back to sequential task arrival, already covered in this topic. One genuinely family of solutions genuinely adds a penalty discouraging large changes to genuinely important earlier weights.
This is already covered generally as regularization in Regularization Techniques, now genuinely protecting specific, important weights, a genuinely direct reuse of that earlier idea.
6. Replay Based Approaches

blocks.alt: Old task examples are replayed during new training

blocks.text: This connects back to regularization based approaches, already covered in this topic. A genuinely different family genuinely keeps a small, stored sample of earlier tasks' own data around.
Genuinely mixing that stored sample back in while training on the genuinely new task, refreshing old memories, a genuinely intuitive, effective alternative explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 7. Architectural Approaches

blocks.alt: Shared layers stay while task-specific layers are added

blocks.text: This connects back to replay based approaches, already covered in this topic. A genuinely third family genuinely adds new, dedicated capacity to the network for each genuinely new task.
Genuinely keeping earlier tasks' own dedicated parameters completely untouched and genuinely protected, a genuinely structural solution explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 8. Stability Plasticity Tradeoff

This connects back to architectural approaches, already covered in this topic. Genuinely every continual learning method genuinely balances stability, keeping old knowledge, against plasticity, learning new tasks.
Genuinely leaning too far either direction genuinely causes forgetting or genuinely causes an inability to learn anything new, the exact core tension explored throughout the rest of this topic.
9. Recognizing When Continual Learning Is Genuinely Necessary

blocks.alt: A model needing to keep learning new tasks over time points toward continual learning

blocks.text: This connects back to sequential task arrival, already covered in this topic. Continual learning, already covered in this topic, genuinely suits models that must keep adapting to new tasks over time.

This connects back to a genuinely fixed, unchanging task with all data available upfront, already covered generally in Supervised Fine-Tuning. Ordinary training, already covered generally, remains genuinely simpler and sufficient for one fixed, stable task.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates a simplified regularization-based approach, already covered in this topic, penalizing large changes to important weights.

code.content:
def continual_training_step(current_weight, new_task_gradient, important_weight, penalty_strength=0.5, learning_rate=0.1):
    # already covered as regularization based approaches in this topic
    forgetting_penalty = penalty_strength * (current_weight - important_weight)
    total_gradient = new_task_gradient + forgetting_penalty
    return current_weight - learning_rate * total_gradient

# already covered as a weight important to an earlier task in this topic
important_weight_from_task_1 = 0.8
current_weight = important_weight_from_task_1

# already covered as new task gradients arriving sequentially in this topic
new_task_gradients = [0.3, 0.25, 0.2]

print(f"Weight after task 1, considered genuinely important (already covered in this topic): {current_weight}")
for step, gradient in enumerate(new_task_gradients):
    current_weight = continual_training_step(current_weight, gradient, important_weight_from_task_1)
    print(f"After task 2, step {step + 1} (already covered as regularization in this topic): weight = {current_weight:.4f}")

print(f"\nFinal weight still stays genuinely close to the original important value, {important_weight_from_task_1},")
print("rather than drifting far away, exactly the forgetting prevention already covered in this topic")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Continual learning lets a model keep learning new tasks without forgetting old ones.
It exists specifically to systematically solve the catastrophic forgetting risk already covered elsewhere.
Real settings present tasks one after another, without revisiting earlier tasks' full original data.
Regularization based approaches penalize large changes to weights important for earlier tasks.
Replay based approaches mix a small stored sample of old data back into new training.
Architectural approaches add new, dedicated capacity per task, protecting old parameters entirely.
Every method balances stability, keeping old knowledge, against plasticity, learning new tasks.
Continual learning suits models that must keep adapting; ordinary training suits one fixed task.
